messages:
alena: Heads-up — last night's CI bench kicked off a golden-alert for kernel selector P95 on the small-seq workload. ~12% regression vs baseline.
rico: saw that. graph looks noisy though, a couple spikes during KV warmup window.
samir: link to the panel? I want to see apples-to-apples overlay.
alena: https://dash.redwood/internal/bench/seq-small — compare commit ab12 -> ab45, same model, same machine type.
dawn: bench-bot posted an alert: `bench-bot: ALERT kernel_selector_p95 > 10% threshold` at 02:14 UTC
marta: quick hypothesis — we switched the batching heuristic last week (dynamic-slice-v2). Could be slightly different latency distribution for short sequences.
rico: also kv-cache hit patterns changed in the replay harness after we added prefix compression. That can move the cold-start window.
samir: can we reproduce locally with the replay harness pinned to the same trace? command I use:
```
./harness/replay --trace traces/small-seq-2026-03.gz --kernel-policy dynamic-slice-v2 --seed 42 --out /tmp/out.json
```
rico: repro'd with seed 42 — I see median within 1% but P95 jumps ~10-13% intermittently. adding jitter to request spacing smooths it out.
alena: important: our CI apples-to-apples runner currently uses median-based gating. That hides P95 regressions. We should run both median and tail SLOs in the nightly.
dawn: +1. also want deterministic KV warmup: add pre-warm trace or synthetic prefix to stabilize cold-cache variance.
marta: idea: compute a "stability score" across N runs (e.g., 5 runs) where score = 1 - (stddev(P95)/mean(P95)). If score < 0.7, mark flaky and don't auto-bisect.
samir: love that. bench-bot can run 3 quick retries when a threshold is crossed, publish jittered-run results to the dash and only open alert if median of retries still breaches.
rico: for alerting, flip from absolute >10% to a two-stage rule: (1) quick retry check, (2) if persistent then open ticket to eng-runtime and post to #eng-sre and #eng-runtime-oncall.
alena: need to be careful with cost. running 3 retries on every alert multiplies CI time. limit to nightly-only alerts, keep PR checks cheap.
dawn: automation tasks:
- add P95 and P99 to apples-to-apples gating
- implement stability score and flaky suppression
- bench-bot retry logic + annotate dashboard with run ids
- synthetic pre-warm for KV cache experiments
- publish a short runbook for triage
marta: I'll own the bench-bot retry patch. planning to add a new metric tag `flakiness_score` in the run metadata.
samir: I'll work on synthetic pre-warm and a small harness change to log per-request KV hit rates so we can correlate tail latency with cache behavior.
rico: I'll update the alerting rules in terraform and add the two-stage rule. also add an email to eng-runtime-oncall for persistent incidents.
alena: short-term mitigation: revert dynamic-slice-v2 on the small-seq profile, run nightly to validate. If P95 improves consistently, we can iterate on a better heuristic.
bench-bot: ACTION log: enqueued retry job 1880012345-try1 for ab45 -> will post results to /dash/bench/1880012345
marta: thanks — will post a PR with bench-bot changes today. tagging @dawn for runbook review.
dawn: I'll draft the runbook: triage steps, priority for KV-related regressions, how to interpret stability_score, and when to escalate.
alena: cool. timeline: aim to have bench-bot retry + stability score in the next 72h, run a 3-night smoke to confirm baseline, then flip alerting rule if stable.
samir: one more: add a small fuzz test in CI that injects 0-10ms inter-request jitter for synthetic loads. That catches heuristics that are overly sensitive to perfect spacing.
ico: thanks all, appreciate quick triage. :thumbsup:
